name: bash
description: Run a shell command in the workspace root. Output is truncated if long; the command is killed on timeout. Use this for running commands (builds, tests, git); when a dedicated tool fits, prefer it over the bash equivalent — grep/glob/keyword_search to search, read_file to read — they stay inside the workspace boundary and give better results. There is no TTY: interactive commands (`git rebase -i`, editors, REPLs, prompts) hang until killed. Do not commit, push, or create branches unless the user asks.

background.description: Run the command in the background: returns a work handle immediately; the result arrives as a message when it finishes.

notify.description: For background work only: when its outcome flows back to you as a message. 'always' (default), 'on_fail' (only when it fails), or 'none' (fire-and-forget: no message, the result is not retrievable — use only when you genuinely do not need the outcome).
